      This variable was used prior to 2.1.x to indicate that OpenJPA should attempt to use a Reader-based JDBC 4.0 method to set Clob or XML data. It allowed XMLType and Clob values larger than 4000 bytes to be used. For 2.1.x+, code was added to allow said functionality by default (see OPENJPA-1691). For forward compatibility, this variable should not be removed.

    • getExtractDateTimeFieldFunction

      public String getExtractDateTimeFieldFunction(DateTimeExtractField extField)
      Oracle has no EXTRACT(QUARTER) or EXTRACT(WEEK); both are read from TO_CHAR, IW being the ISO week that JPA defines. EXTRACT(HOUR/MINUTE/SECOND) is only allowed on TIMESTAMP values, whereas temporal values are usually held in DATE columns, so the value is cast to TIMESTAMP. EXTRACT(SECOND) then includes the fraction of the second, as JPA requires. The cast also drops the time zone of a TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE value, such as an OffsetDateTime, so its hour and minute are those of the stored offset, as OffsetDateTime.getHour() returns them, and no longer those in UTC.
      Overrides:
      getExtractDateTimeFieldFunction in class DBDictionary

    • getExtractDateTimePartFunction

      public String getExtractDateTimePartFunction(DateTimeExtractPart part)
      An Oracle DATE has a time of day and there is no TIME type, so CAST(x AS DATE) would keep the time and CAST(x AS TIME) is invalid. The date is truncated to midnight instead, and the time is the time of day on 1970-01-01, as times are stored and bound. As a time is held in a DATE, it has whole seconds only, so the fraction of the second of a TIMESTAMP value is dropped. The value occurs twice in the SQL of the time, so a parameter is bound twice.
      Overrides:
      getExtractDateTimePartFunction in class DBDictionary
